state_entity.regulator: New York Department of Financial Services
state_entity.status: Circle's Q2 2026 results say it received approval from NYDFS to open Circle New York Trust; the current Circle licenses page lists the entity as chartered.
state_entity.issuer_role: The retrieved current license page does not establish that this entity is presently the USDC issuer. Circle's 2025 OCC application described a plan to transition USDC issuance to a New York limited-purpose trust company; current Circle disclosures say USDC is issued by regulated affiliates.

federal_entity.legal_name: First National Digital Currency Bank, N.A.
federal_entity.approved_initial_scope: Upon opening, fiduciary digital-asset custody for Circle and affiliates.
federal_entity.future_scope: Management of the USDC Reserve is described by Circle as a future capability. Direct custody for a limited number of institutional clients is demand-dependent and not represented as active at launch.

state_entity.regulator: New York Department of Financial Services
state_entity.role: RLUSD issuer, according to Ripple's October 26, 2026 announcement.

state_entity.regulator: New York Department of Financial Services
state_entity.role: Existing state-chartered custody entity; separate from Coinbase National Trust Company.

federal_entity.migration_note: OCC Corporate Decision 1370 describes a proposed migration plan over time; it does not establish that the state-chartered custody entity has already been replaced or that the federal bank is operational.

comparison.coinbase_federal_status: Approved on 2026-04-02; no Consummated/Effective row visible in retrieved CAS record
comparison.key_distinction: The state limited-purpose trust companies and federal national trust banks are separate legal entities under different regulators. A federal charter status must not be conflated with an existing NYDFS custody charter.
comparison.nydfs_lp_trust_limitations: NYDFS describes limited-purpose trust companies as not receiving deposits from the general public and generally not making loans except as incidental to fiduciary powers. This statement applies to the state LP trust-company category, not automatically to the OCC national trust-bank entities.
comparison.circle_bank_scope: Circle says custody for Circle and affiliates is the initial service upon opening; USDC reserve management is a future capability, and direct institutional custody is demand-dependent.
comparison.ripple_bank_scope: Ripple describes reserve management, collateral-trustee functions and fiduciary custody upon opening; current operating/customer volumes are not established.
comparison.coinbase_bank_scope: The federal Coinbase National Trust application is approved but not shown as consummated/effective in the retrieved CAS record. Coinbase's separate NYDFS Coinbase Custody Trust Company remains listed.

issuer_separation.usdc: USDC is issued by Circle-regulated affiliates. Do not assume Circle National Trust itself issues USDC. Circle's 2025 application described a planned transition to a NY limited-purpose trust company; current retrieved disclosures do not identify the exact current issuing legal entity.
issuer_separation.rlusd: Standard Custody & Trust Company, LLC remains RLUSD issuer; Ripple National Trust Bank is a separate federal trust-bank entity.

xrp_relevance.shared_bny_provider_relationship: Separate Circle/USDC and Ripple/RLUSD relationships with BNY do not establish a direct Circle-Ripple partnership.
xrp_relevance.forecast_use: Regulatory and entity-structure context only; not a directional XRP feature without measured adoption/flow and out-of-sample evidence.
